promises.opening: Good evening, everyone. So, if you look at the quarter, what we spoke about earlier, revenue grew at a rate of 6.4% on a Y-o-Y basis. This is when the festive season, as you know, has shifted entirely to Q3. So, one should look at when you look at Q2, Q3, depending on when the festivals are, one should look at Q2 and Q3 together. So, a lot of impact of the sales with September, the festival season shifted to Q3. We see strong growth in Q3 there. Registered customer base was up 10% on a Y-o-Y basis. It is crossed 400 million. Transactions have grown in line with revenue growth of 7%. All our consumption baskets have grown, so growth is quite broad based. We opened 303 new stores. Net adds is 200 lower because we also shut down 500 stores. So, we have shut down some of the unviable stores. We are looking at a transition where we will open those under some of the formats that we are opening because real estate is difficult to get in India. But that will take two, three quarters to transition them to the newer formats. EBITDA margin, when you look at it, is 7.8%. EBITDA of Rs.6,228 Crores. This is before a one-time exceptional charge on account of 7-eleven of Rs.108 Crores because as you might have seen in the news, we have shut down the 7-eleven format. If you look at the margin trajectory, it is consistent with last few quarters of the operating EBITDA as well as the 6 © Reliance Industries Limited 2020 reported EBITDA is down just 10 basis points and that is more the festive impact because the pull in the festival season you see most of the full price sales. So, the margin trajectory is consistent with last couple of quarters. And what we have seen as we have grown our online business, margins have come down, and that is the nature of the online business. We are going very strong on growing our digital commerce business. The online scale up is happening as planned. We had discussed last time that we are setting up a lot of infrastructure. We made a conscious call. To significantly grow our online business, invest in the infrastructure and the technology there and the benefits of that scale will come in the next couple of years. So, this year is the year of investment. So, if you look at how we are progressing on that, I think that progress is happening quite well. Online while we are doing with discipline with the right unit economics. If you look at the early shots grocery, online revenue has grown 42% on a Y-o-Y basis. The share of online in both grocery and electronics is growing pretty steadily. So, I think the progress is quite good. And next couple of years, as the business scales up and starts contributing meaningfully to our overall scale, while individually the businesses are meaningful, but in the context of our overall revenue of Rs.90,000 Crores, they are still small. As they grow, the benefits of the scale will start reflecting in the absolute EBITDA numbers. A few macro trends. I guess most of you are aware. Inflation is on a two year high, which is impacting the purchasing power for people. Currency has depreciated significantly. That is impacting, especially, some of the imported products. The landed products have gone up. Monsoon deficit. So that has caused some demand pressure across some of the key agri dependent states, as well as the food prices are moving up. So that is also eating into the discretionary demand. And then the festive calendar we spoke about compared to last year, this time. The festivals have started purely in October, so October is reflecting that. And Q3 you will see the full impact of the festival. Just to recap our scale, we have the largest retail platform in the country, spanning 400 million plus subscribers, close to 20,000 stores. Retail area is 77.5 million square feet, so it is roughly a million square feet lower because of closure of the stores.
